current_leader.name: Cloud support-plan right-sizing engine
current_leader.state_transition: monthly cloud spend + provider-independent workload criticality/SLO/incident telemetry -> recompute support-plan cost and required support capabilities -> compare eligible tiers/substitutes -> recommend KEEP/DOWNGRADE/UPGRADE -> verify support-fee delta
current_leader.why_survived: The immediately prior run rejected the card-authorization integrity-fee wedge after finding enterprise OMS layers that already automate fulfillment-aware authorization reversals. Cloud support-plan right-sizing therefore remains the best survivor. Fresh research confirms AWS paid support remains monthly/changeable and exposes explicit plan comparison/pricing tools, while no exact continuous cross-cloud engine was found that combines SLO/incident criticality with support-plan economics. The wedge remains read-only and fee deltas are deterministic, but plan consolidation and partner-led support increase substitution risk.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: AWS documents monthly support tiers, self-service plan changes and pricing calculators; Enterprise self-service enrollment has no long-term commitment. AWS will discontinue Developer, Business and Enterprise On-Ramp on January 1, 2027, reducing tier variety. DoiT offers partner-led enterprise support economics, showing that support can be substituted rather than only downgraded. No exact telemetry-aware cross-cloud support-tier optimizer surfaced in current searches.
current_leader.closest_threat: AWS first-party compare/pricing/change workflows, 2026-2027 support-plan migrations, partner-led support substitutes such as DoiT, and broad FinOps/MSP services. WhatPlan already simulates AWS support-plan pricing but does not determine operational sufficiency.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read billing forecast, current support tier, workload criticality/SLOs, incident history and required response-time/features; recommend the cheapest sufficient native or partner-led support option with exact fee delta and capabilities lost/gained; no plan-change execution.
current_leader.monetization: Small accepted-change fee, low monitoring fee, or capped share of verified support-fee savings; performance pricing only if decisions recur more frequently than an annual review.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The economically correct tier may be mostly static and tail-risk-driven. Fewer AWS support tiers and stronger Business Support+ capabilities can further reduce decision frequency, while partner-led substitutes may turn the problem into procurement rather than a programmable micro-decision.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find real customer/MSP support-plan change histories and quantify change frequency plus savings. Test whether workload criticality/spend changes alter the cheapest sufficient option often enough for continuous monitoring. Reject/demote if decisions are predominantly annual or already bundled into broader FinOps/MSP services.

recent_cross_family_findings: Card authorization integrity-fee prevention remains rejected after the prior run found IBM Sterling OMS and Adyen Salesforce OMS fulfillment-aware authorization reversal automation; searching only PSP features had overstated whitespace.

Cloud support-plan right-sizing remains leader at 46/60. AWS plan consolidation effective January 1, 2027 and partner-led support substitutes increase recurrence/substitution risk but do not yet establish an exact telemetry-aware optimizer.
Authorization-validity batch-close timing is rejected because TD explicitly closes batches after 48 hours where possible to avoid Mastercard's 72-hour fee, demonstrating first-party absorption.

Generic prepaid cloud/API credit refund-expiry monitoring is rejected because provider rights are fragmented and usually self-service/non-refundable/non-expiring; it overlaps prior broad entitlement lessons.
Generic music royalty reconciliation/recovery is rejected because current products already ingest statements, reconcile royalties and offer success-fee recovery/metadata repair.
New rule: search OMS/business-system automation, not only PSP-native features, before declaring payment-lifecycle whitespace.
New rule: for cloud support optimization, simple price comparison is not whitespace; only repeated telemetry-driven support sufficiency remains worth testing.
New rule: provider plan consolidation can reduce recurring decision frequency even when the underlying money flow remains large.
